title: Pre-allocating Memory Based on Untrusted Length Header
pattern: Calling allocation functions that reserve capacity (e.g., `Vec::with_capacity`, `String::with_capacity`, `HashSet::with_capacity`) using a numeric variable parsed directly from untrusted input (such as network packet headers or deserialization streams) without first verifying that it is within safe bounds.
why_bad: A malicious or malformed packet can specify a massive length header (e.g., 2GB). Pre-allocating memory based on this untrusted value will trigger an immediate, massive allocation attempt, crashing the process instantly via a panic or OOM abort even if the client never sends a single byte [59].
detection: Identify allocations that take variables parsed from stream/file deserialization or network packet bytes as capacity inputs without sanity check limits.
fix: Validate length fields against a reasonable application-specific maximum threshold before invoking allocation functions [59].
source: Brendan Gregg, *Systems Performance*, Chapter 7 (Memory) / passage [59]; Alex Petrov, *Database Internals*, Chapter 8 / passage [50].
